newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank sets repo at unchanged 4.95 pct.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank sets repo at unchanged 4.95 pct.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, on Tuesday set a new seven-day reverse repurchase operation at an unchanged fixed rate of 4.95 percent.
The operation will run from October 16 until October 23 with bids to be received by 0800 GMT on October 15.
A Reuters poll on Monday found nine out of 11 analysts questioned had not expected a change in the repo rate in the weekly tender.
Two analysts, however, had predicted the central bank would move to again trim its key interest rate, which is its main tool for controlling liquidity in the money market.
This year, the bank has trimmed the repo rate every second week for a total 21 cuts since January from 8.91 percent.
But last week, deputy Riksbank governor Lars Heikensten said the bank did not necessarily have to follow a certain pattern in the future.
This comment caused some confusion on the market, according to analysts, and prompted some speculation about this week's repo operation.

The repo rate is the centre of the Riksbank's three-tiered system with the floor of its interest rate corridor, the deposit rate, currently standing at 4.75 percent and the ceiling, the lending rate, at 6.25 percent.
The lending and deposit rates were last lowered on August 15.
